name: SparseGPT: Massive Language Models Can Be Accurately Pruned in One-Shot
problem: One-shot pruning of 100B+ parameter LLMs to 50% sparsity was thought to require retraining or intractable second-order computation.
mechanism: OBS-style layerwise pruning: for each linear layer compute the inverse second-moment matrix of the inputs (H = 2XX^T) from a small calibration set, Cholesky-factorize it, and prune weights in Cholesky order using the same layerwise error-compensation structure as GPTQ, choosing per-column which weights to zero so the layer-output error stays minimal. Because the pruning decision compensates for itself across columns, no weight reconstruction or iterative solver is needed - and it composes with quantization, so a model can be pruned AND quantized in the same pass.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): first demonstration that GPT-family models can be pruned to at least 50% SPARSITY IN ONE SHOT with no retraining and minimal accuracy loss; 60% UNSTRUCTURED sparsity with 'negligible increase in perplexity' - more than 100 BILLION weights ignorable at inference; executes on OPT-175B and BLOOM-176B IN UNDER 4.5 HOURS. COMPRESSION RATIO: 2x at 50% sparsity, 2.5x at 60%. QUALITY COST: 'negligible increase in perplexity' at 60% unstructured - note that 60% UNSTRUCTORED has no hardware speedup at all on any shipping accelerator, so the compression ratio here is a memory number only. The method also generalizes to 2:4 and 4:8, which is where it becomes a speedup.
